source_text:
17 Εἰ δὲ διὰ τῆς τοῦ Χριστοῦ ἐπιφανείας εἰς τὸν παράδεισον τὸ τῶν
ἀνθρώπων εἰσάγει γένος, ὁπηνίκα δὲ ἐσταυρώθη τὸν λῃστὴν αὐθήμερον εἰσάξειν αὐτόθι προηγόρευσεν τοῦ σώματος ἔτι βεβλημένου τῷ μνήματι, συνέστηκεν ὅτι συνδιαιτωμένη κυρίως ἡ ψυχὴ τοῦ Χριστοῦ τῷ Λόγῳ καὶ Θεῷ, τῷ πᾶσαν ὁμοῦ τὴν τῶν γενητῶν περιέχοντι κτίσιν, τὴν ὁμογενῆ τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ψυχὴν εἰς τὸν παράδεισον εἰσήγαγεν. Οὐδὲ γάρ ἐστι γεγραμμένον ὅτι πρὸ τῆς ἀναστάσεως τοῦ ἁγίου σώματος τὸ τοῦ λῃστοῦ προηγέρθη σῶμα τὴν ἐπαγγελίαν ἀπολαβόν. Ἀκόλουθον ἄρα ἐστὶν ὑπολαμβάνειν ἐμφρόνως ὅτι ἡ ψυχὴ τὴν συγγενῆ ψυχὴν ὁδηγοῦσα φιλοφρόνως, ἅτε δὴ καὶ μείζονος ἐξουσίας ἐχομένη, τὴν μὲν ὑπόσχεσιν αὐθήμερον ἐπὶ πέρας ἦγεν, εἰς δὲ τὴν ἐξαίρετον εἰσῆγε κληρονομίαν ἀνοίγουσα τὸν παράδεισον.
thought_title: Christ's soul led the thief's soul into paradise
orientation: Eustathius is closing his argument that Christ possessed a real human soul, now using the promise to the thief on the cross as proof that Christ's soul, united to the Word, entered paradise while his body still lay in the tomb.
pass_a_gloss: But if through the appearing of Christ he leads the race of humans into paradise, and at the time when he was crucified he foretold that he would lead the thief in there that very day, while the body was still cast into the tomb, it has been established that the soul of Christ, dwelling together properly with the Word and God [the same divine person the Arians call 'the Spirit'], who encompasses all at once the creation of things that have come to be, led the kindred soul of the human into paradise. For it is not written that before the resurrection of the holy body the body of the thief was brought forward, having received the promise. It is reasonable therefore to suppose sensibly that the soul, guiding the kindred soul kindly, inasmuch as it also held greater authority, was bringing the promise to fulfillment that very day, and was leading it into the special inheritance, opening paradise.

choices.why: Keeps the literal sense of Christ's manifestation or coming, without importing later theological weight of 'epiphany' as a feast.
Renders the compound verb literally and keeps the adverb 'properly' to mark the true union of Christ's soul with the Word, which is the point against the Arians.

choices.english: the kindred soul of the human
choices.why: Preserves the kinship language ('same kind') that Eustathius uses to stress that Christ's soul and the thief's soul share one human nature.
rejected: the soul of the same race as the human

choices.why: The imperfect with 'to the end' conveys ongoing completion of the promise that very day, matching the source's aspect.
Keeps the adjective's sense of 'chosen out' or 'exceptional' for paradise as the inheritance, without over-interpreting as 'heavenly'.

pass_b_english: But if through the appearing of Christ the human race is being brought into paradise, and if at the hour he was crucified he foretold that he would bring the thief there that very day while his body still lay cast into the tomb, then it is established that the soul of Christ, dwelling together properly with the Word and God who encompasses all created things at once, brought the kindred soul of the man into paradise. For it is nowhere written that before the resurrection of the holy body the thief's body went ahead and received the promise. It follows, then, to think sensibly that the soul, kindly guiding the kindred soul, since it indeed possessed the greater authority, was bringing the promise to fulfillment that very day, and was leading it into the special inheritance, opening paradise.

problems.quote: the kindred soul of the human
problems.why: "τοῦ ἀνθρώπου" is genitive singular, "of the man/human being"—the thief's soul, not "the human" as generic.
problems.fix: the kindred soul of the man

problems.quote: the soul, guiding the kindred soul kindly
problems.source_quote: ἡ ψυχὴ τὴν συγγενῆ ψυχὴν ὁδηγοῦσα φιλοφρόνως
problems.why: "φιλοφρόνως" modifies the action of guiding, not the soul itself; "kindly guiding" or "with kindly intent."
problems.fix: the soul, kindly guiding the kindred soul

problems.why: The source refers to the thief's soul (singular), not a generic 'kindred soul'.
problems.fix: the soul of the same kind
problems.ruling: τὴν συγγενῆ ψυχὴν refers to the thief's soul specifically (antecedent λῃστοῦ), not generic 'kindred soul'.

edits.old: the kindred soul of the human
edits.new: the kindred soul of the man

edits.old: the soul, guiding the kindred soul kindly
edits.new: the soul, kindly guiding the kindred soul
the soul of the same kind

problems.quote: the tabernacle of the Word and God
problems.why: Reader may not realize 'tabernacle,' 'body,' 'flesh' all refer to same thing.
problems.fix: Consistently gloss 'tabernacle' as 'body' or add note.

variants.text: the tabernacle of the Word and God

problems.quote: the soul, kindly guiding the kindred soul
problems.why: 'Kindly' is weak; likely means 'as kin/of same nature' (Greek syngenes).
problems.fix: Use 'as kin' or 'the kindred soul, guiding its kin'.

problems.why: Unclear what 'special' means; likely 'peculiar/proper inheritance' (Greek idios).

edits.old: the soul, kindly guiding the kindred soul
edits.new: the soul, guiding the kindred soul as kin

fixed: The glossary issue about 'tabernacle' is not present in this section; no edit needed.
The mistranslation of 'kindly' is fixed by rendering it as 'as kin' to reflect the Greek syngenes.
The mistranslation of 'special inheritance' is fixed by rendering it as 'its own inheritance' to reflect the Greek idios.

problems.quote: the tabernacle of the Word and God
problems.why: Reader may not realize 'tabernacle,' 'body,' and 'holy body' all refer to Christ's physical body.

variants.text: the tabernacle of the Word and God

problems.why: Arians attribute passions to 'the Spirit' but Eustathius uses 'Word'—reader may miss these are the same divine person.

problems.quote: the soul, guiding the kindred soul as kin
problems.why: Repetition of 'kindred/kin' is awkward; 'kindred soul' and 'as kin' may confuse reader about whether thief is literal relative.
problems.fix: Clarify 'kindred' means 'of the same human nature,' not family relation.

edits.old: the soul, guiding the kindred soul as kin
edits.new: the soul, guiding the kindred soul as one of the same nature

fixed: The glossary problem about 'tabernacle' is not present in this section; the English uses 'body' and 'holy body,' not 'tabernacle.'
The glossary problem about 'the Spirit' is not present in this section; the English uses 'Word and God.'

last_rejected.why: Glossary requires 'tabernacle' for σκηνή-related concepts; 'dwelling together' violates glossary for σκηνή/συνδιαιτωμένη.
last_rejected.ruling: συνδιαιτωμένη from συνδιαίω, not σκηνή; 'dwelling together' is correct range, no glossary violation.

last_rejected.why: English says 'the promise' was brought to fulfillment, but source says 'τὴν μὲν ὑπόσχεσιν'—the promise to the thief, not 'the promise' as abstract.
last_rejected.fix: was bringing his promise to fulfillment that very day
last_rejected.ruling: τὴν ὑπόσχεσιν is 'the promise'; article marks known promise. English captures meaning adequately.

last_rejected.why: English 'opening paradise' lacks object; source has 'τὸν παράδεισον' as object of 'opening', but English makes it ambiguous whether paradise is being opened or entered.
last_rejected.ruling: English 'opening paradise' includes 'paradise' as object; no omission or ambiguity exists.
